title: The Frozen Event Loop
subtitle: One innocent call stalls every async request

brief.narrative: An async FastAPI handler calls a synchronous SDK that blocks for three seconds. Event-loop lag rises and unrelated requests stop progressing.
symptoms: FastAPI Event Loop metrics diverge from the service-level symptom
The problem reproduces only under the triggering workload
Logs contain enough evidence to distinguish cause from consequence
brief.objective: Identify the root cause, select a production-safe fix, and explain the trade-off.

rootCause.question: Which root cause explains all of the evidence?

options.text: The failure boundary is a process, not a thread; memory is isolated between processes.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: A data race on a non-atomic shared counter caused lost increments.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: Opposite lock ordering created a circular wait.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: Blocking I/O ran directly on the event-loop thread.
options.feedback: Correct. async improves concurrency only when tasks yield. Unbounded offloading can merely move saturation to a thread pool.

fix.question: Which fix is safest for production?

options.text: Use an atomic primitive or lock around the minimal critical section, or remove shared mutable state through partitioning/message passing.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: Define a global lock order, acquire in that order, keep lock scope small, and use timeouts only as a recovery safety net.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: Use an async client, move blocking calls to a bounded thread pool, set timeouts, and monitor event-loop lag.
options.feedback: Correct. async improves concurrency only when tasks yield. Unbounded offloading can merely move saturation to a thread pool.
